title: 2026_PMC13100012_Coverage_and_associated_factors_of_inactivated_polio_vaccine_up
ehr_evidence: A secondary data analysis was conducted using data from the recent demographic and health survey in 20 SSA countries between 2016 and 2023. The source was the Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) kids' record (KR) file, a population-based household survey using mother/caretaker verbal reports and vaccination cards, not an EHR.
summary: A multilevel cross-sectional secondary analysis of DHS data assessing inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) coverage and its socio-demographic and healthcare-access determinants among 43,564 weighted children aged 12-23 months across 20 Sub-Saharan African countries.
key_findings: Pooled IPV coverage was 65.10% (95% CI: 55.44, 74.76), below the WHO herd-immunity threshold of 90% and the 2024 global coverage of 85%.
Maternal age 20-34 years (AOR=1.08, 95% CI: 1.00, 1.18) and ≥35 years (AOR=1.22, 95% CI: 1.11, 1.34) were associated with higher IPV odds versus mothers aged 15-19.
Maternal primary education (AOR=1.30, 95% CI: 1.23, 1.37) and secondary-or-above (AOR=1.87, 95% CI: 1.76, 1.99) increased odds versus no formal education.
Rich household wealth showed an inverse association (AOR=0.84, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.89) versus poor households.
Married (AOR=0.83, 95% CI: 0.75, 0.90) and widowed/divorced/separated (AOR=0.85, 95% CI: 0.75, 0.95) mothers had lower odds versus single mothers.

Media exposure (AOR=1.20, 95% CI: 1.14, 1.25), ≥4 ANC visits (AOR=2.51, 95% CI: 2.33, 2.70), health-facility delivery (AOR=1.86, 95% CI: 1.77, 1.97), PNC (AOR=1.73, 95% CI: 1.65, 1.82), birth interval >48 months (AOR=1.34, 95% CI: 1.24, 1.44), urban residence (AOR=1.24, 95% CI: 1.17, 1.31), and high community women literacy (AOR=1.68, 95% CI: 1.54, 1.83) were positive determinants.
Regional odds versus Central Africa were higher in Eastern Africa (AOR=3.67, 95% CI: 3.22, 4.19), Western Africa (AOR=4.86, 95% CI: 4.27, 5.53), and Southern Africa (AOR=8.41, 95% CI: 7.08, 9.99).
Cluster-level variation accounted for ~6.4% of total variance (ICC=0.064) with a median odds ratio of 1.96 (95% CI: 1.88, 2.04).
study_design: Cross-sectional secondary (multilevel logistic regression) analysis of pooled survey data
population: 43,564 weighted children aged 12-23 months and their mothers across 20 Sub-Saharan African countries (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cote d'Ivoire, Ethiopia, Gabon, Ghana, Gambia, Guinea, Kenya, Liberia, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritania, Mozambique, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda)
exposure_domain: Vaccine-uptake determinants (socio-demographic, maternal health-service use, household wealth, community literacy/media, and geographic factors)
limitations: Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference between exposures and IPV uptake.
Reliance on mother/caretaker verbal reports alongside vaccination cards may introduce recall bias.
Possible time lag between data collection and release, so data may not reflect the most recent changes.
data_availability_statement: The datasets generated and analyzed for the present study are available in the DHS website (which is available from https://dhsprogram.com/data/available-datasets.cfm).
